meta.title: Xnapper Case Study — Nahuel Uliassi Pirchio
meta.description: How I took Xnapper from a screenshot tool to a full video editing product — video pipeline, licensing backend, architecture and reliability, end to end.

header.summary: Over sixteen months, I worked across the different layers of Xnapper: editing interfaces, application logic and state, multimedia processing, persistence and backend services for a commercial product with approximately 20,000 users.

paragraphs: Xnapper is a commercial screenshot tool that expanded into image and video editing. As a Software Developer on the team, I owned features across the interface, application state, processing, persistence and service integrations — not a single layer of the stack.

The technical difficulty came from moving beyond static screenshot editing into frame-accurate video workflows that had to stay reliable and maintainable across different runtime environments, without sacrificing performance.

blocks.title: Frontend and product experience
blocks.body: Built editing interfaces with React and Next.js: timeline, clip manipulation, playback and export controls.

blocks.title: Application state and logic
blocks.body: Modeled editor state, undo/redo history and session/preset persistence, connecting interface behavior to the product's different workflows.

blocks.title: Processing
blocks.body: Implemented video processing with Node.js, FFmpeg and WebAssembly, coordinating files, playback, progress and output generation.

blocks.title: Backend and data
blocks.body: Designed and shipped a serverless licensing service that enforced per-device business rules and persisted activation state in Redis.

challenge.statement: The product needed to move beyond static screenshot editing and support reliable video workflows without sacrificing performance, maintainability or consistency across environments.

built.title: Video editing pipeline
built.intro: Built this capability end to end: from timeline interactions and state modeling to frame extraction, processing and final export.
bullets: Designed the interface and interactions for timeline, clips and playhead.
Modeled editing state, clip normalization and undo/redo history.
Built frame-accurate playback and seeking.
Implemented processing and export with FFmpeg/WASM.
Integrated progress, cancellation, error handling and final file generation.

built.title: Authentication & integrations
bullets: Implemented the Google OAuth authentication flow for both the web app and the desktop application.
Hardened session handling and renewal to keep product flows authenticated.

built.title: Backend licensing service
built.intro: Designed and shipped a serverless backend to validate commercial licenses and control how many devices could be associated with each user.
bullets: Built the validation endpoint with Node.js and Express, deployed as a serverless function.
Modeled licenses and active devices on top of Upstash Redis.
Enforced per-device seat limit rules.
Implemented idempotent activation to avoid duplicate records on repeated validation calls.
Handled soft-delete device removal without losing activation history.

built.title: Product state & architecture
bullets: Export Strategy abstraction
Undo/redo history based on the Memento pattern
Session and preset persistence
Cross-runtime behavior consistency

built.title: Reliability & security
bullets: Safer file and path handling
Reduced local-server attack surface
Removal of unsafe process integrations
Automated tests for critical paths

decisions.title: Demuxer-based frame extraction
decisions.problem: Native video seeking wasn't reliable on variable-frame-rate footage — a seek could land on the wrong frame, breaking frame-accurate editing.
decisions.approach: Extracted frames through a demuxer instead of relying on native seek, giving the editor a consistent, frame-accurate source regardless of a clip's original encoding.

decisions.title: Export strategies
decisions.problem: Supporting multiple export targets was spreading conditional logic across the codebase, making every new export option riskier to add.
decisions.approach: Introduced a shared export strategy interface so each target implements the same contract, keeping the branching logic in one place instead of scattered conditionals.

decisions.title: Idempotent activation model
decisions.problem: The client could validate the same license repeatedly, and an already-active device shouldn't duplicate its record or consume more than one available seat.
decisions.approach: Designed activation as an idempotent operation: if the device was already active, the service returned success without duplicating the record. Deactivations were modeled with soft-delete to preserve history without consuming an available seat.

items: Expanded the product from screenshot-focused workflows into video editing.
Shipped the work through multiple production releases.
Improved maintainability of export and persistence flows.
Reduced important security and reliability risks.
Supported a product used by approximately 20,000 users.
